signals.title: [Data] Ray Data CBO (Cost-Based Optimizer) Design
signals.text: ### Description ## 1. Background and Motivation ### 1.1 Problem Statement Ray Data currently uses a purely Rule-Based Optimizer (RBO). All optimization rules are executed in a fixed topological order, with no awareness of data statistical characteristics. This means the following critical parameters can only be set manually by engineers: - **Reservation ratio** `op_resource_reservation_ratio`: Controls the memory reservation proportion for each operator, defaults to 0.5 - **Shuffle partition count** `num_partitions`: Number of partitions for Join/Sort/Repartition - **Read parallelism**: Number of output blocks for the Read operator ```python # Engineer A's config (long pipeline + GPU mix) ctx.op_resource_reservation_ratio = 0.7 # Engineer B's config (short pipeline + batch inference) ctx.op_resource_reservation_ratio = 0.2 # Engineer C's config (doesn't know what to set, uses default 0.5) ctx.op_resource_reservation_ratio = 0.5 # But 0.5 may be too high or too low, depending on: # - How many operators are in the pipeline? # - What is the data amplification/reduction ratio for each operator? # - Are there GPU operators? # - Are there AllToAll (Sort/Shuffle) operators? # - How severe is the data skew? ``` **Core contradiction**: This information can be derived from data statistical characteristics before execution, but the current RBO is entirely unable to leverage it. ### 1.2 Quantified Impact | Scenario | Issue with default R=0.5 | Ideal R value | |----------|--------------------------|---------------| | Long pipeline (6 operators) + GPU | Insufficient reservation, GPU operators frequently backpressured | 0.6~0.7 | | Short pipeline (2 operators) + batch inference | Over-reservation, resources idle and wasted | 0.2~0.3 | | Sort pipeline (AllToAll) | Upstream reservation meaningless (memory limit lifted) | 0.2~0.3 | | Single-operator-dominated pipeline | Reservation for other operators meaningless | 0.1~0.2 | ### 1.3 Design Goals This proposal designs a CBO (Cost-Based Optimizer) for Ray Data, addressing the following problems: 1. **Auto-derive `reservation_ratio`**: Based on data statistics and cost model, eliminating manual tuning 2. **Auto-derive `num_partitions`**: Adapt Join/Shuffle partition counts to data volume 3. **Automatic Join reordering**: Automatically place the smaller table on the build side for INNER JOINs 4. **Runtime feedback**: Use runtime metrics from previous executions to correct compile-time estimates ### 1.4 Non-Goals (Scope Out) - **SQL optimization**: No subquery unnesting, view rewriting, or other SQL-layer optimizations - **Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)**: No dynamic changes to execution plan topology during execution - **Multi-tenant resource isolation**: No cross-pipeline resource contention awareness - **Column statistics for non-Parquet data sources**: CSV/JSON and other data sources do not support column-level statistics for now --- ## 2. Constraints ### 2.1 Architectural Constraints **C-1: Must use existing Rule/Optimizer/Ruleset interfaces** ```python # Source path: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/interfaces/optimizer.py class Rule: def apply(self, plan: Plan) -> Plan: raise NotImplementedError @classmethod def dependencies(cls) -> List[Type["Rule"]]: return [] # Pre-dependencies @classmethod def dependents(cls) -> List[Type["Rule"]]: return [] # Post-dependents class Optimizer: def optimize(self, plan: Plan) -> Plan: previous_plan = plan while True: for rule in self.rules: plan = rule.apply(plan) if plan.dag.dag_str == previous_plan.dag.dag_str: break # Converged previous_plan = plan return plan ``` All CBO rules must implement the `Rule` interface and register via `Ruleset`. Bypassing the `Optimizer.optimize()` convergence loop is not allowed. **C-2: Three-phase execution pipeline must not be changed** ```python # Source path: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/optimizers.py def get_execution_plan(logical_plan: LogicalPlan) -> PhysicalPlan: # 1. Logical optimization optimized_logical_plan = LogicalOptimizer().optimize(logical_plan) # 2. Plan conversion physical_plan = create_planner().plan(optimized_logical_plan) # 3. Physical optimization return PhysicalOptimizer().optimize(physical_plan) ``` CBO statistics propagation rules should be registered in the logical optimization phase; CBO parameter derivation rules should be registered in the physical optimization phase. **C-3: `ReservationOpResourceAllocator` reservation model must not be changed** ``` Per-operator reservation = M × R / N where M = total resources, R = reservation_ratio, N = number of active operators ``` CBO can only modify the global `R` value (`DataContext.op_resource_reservation_ratio`); it cannot change the reservation formula itself. Half of the reservation goes to internal buffers, half to outputs. ### 2.2 Compatibility Constraints **C-4: Backward compatible — user-explicit settings take priority** CBO-derived values only take effect when the user has **not explicitly set** them. A `_user_set_reservation_ratio` flag needs to be introduced in `DataContext` to distinguish "user intentionally set 0.5" from "used the default 0.5". > Currently there is no such flag in `DataContext` (`grep _user_set` returns empty); it needs to be added. **C-5: Must safely fall back when statistics are unavailable** For non-Parquet data sources, custom Datasources, encrypted data, etc., statistics may be entirely unavailable. CBO must fall back to existing RBO behavior without producing worse results. **C-6: Expressions API is in Alpha stage** Ray Data's expression system (`BinaryExpr`, `ColumnExpr`, `LiteralExpr`, etc.) is annotated with `@DeveloperAPI(stability="alpha")`, and the interface may change. Selectivity estimation logic must be loosely coupled with the Expressions API. ### 2.3 Performance Constraints **C-7: Statistics collection overhead must be far lower than actual execution** Parquet footer reading is already done in `_fetch_parquet_file_info` (zero additional IO). Sampling estimation should be limited to `avg_row_bytes` and schema inference from the first batch of data, and must not trigger additional data reads. **C-8: `get_execution_plan` is a synchronous call that does not tolerate sub-millisecond latency** Statistics propagation and cost calculation must be pure in-memory operations, with no network IO or disk IO allowed. --- ## 3. Current State Analysis ### 3.1 Existing Optimization Rules | Phase | Rule | Type | Uses Statistics | |-------|------|------|:--------------:| | Logical Optimization | `InheritBatchFormatRule` | RBO | No | | Logical Optimization | `LimitPushdownRule` | RBO | No | | Logical Optimization | `ProjectionPushdown` | RBO | No | | Logical Optimization | `PredicatePushdown` | RBO | No | | Logical Optimization | `CombineShuffles` | RBO | No | | Physical Optimization | `InheritTargetMaxBlockSizeRule` | RBO | No | | Physical Optimization | `SetReadParallelismRule` | Estimate | Partial (`size_bytes`) | | Physical Optimization | `FuseOperators` | RBO | No | | Physical Optimization | `ConfigureMapTaskMemoryUsingOutputSize` | Estimate | Partial (`average_bytes_per_output`) | **Key finding**: Two rules already use coarse-grained statistical estimates, but they only use data size — not row counts, selectivity, column-level statistics, skew, or other critical statistics. ### 3.2 Existing Statistics Inventory Ray Data is not entirely without statistics, but they are scattered across multiple modules and not systematically utilized: **Logical layer**: | Source | Statistics | Coverage | |--------|-----------|----------| | `LogicalOperator.infer_metadata()` | `BlockMetadata(num_rows, size_bytes, input_files, exec_stats)` | `Read` and `InputData` have implementations; other operators return `None` | | `LogicalOperator.estimated_num_outputs()` | Estimated output block count | `Read` based on `size_bytes / target_max_block_size` | | `LogicalOperator.infer_schema()` | Output schema | `Read` and some operators have implementations | **Data source layer**: | Source | Statistics | Issue | |--------|-----------|-------| | `_ParquetFileInfo.metadata` | Parquet footer (contains min/max/null_count/distinct_count) | Column-level statistics **entirely unused** | | `_ParquetFileInfo.avg_row_in_mem_bytes` | Average bytes per row in memory | Only used for `estimate_in_memory_bytes()` | **Runtime layer**: | Source | Statistics | Consumer | |--------|-----------|----------| | `OpRuntimeMetrics.average_bytes_per_output` | Average bytes per output block | `ConfigureMapTaskMemoryUsingOutputSize` | | `OpRuntimeMetrics.rows_task_outputs_generated` | Output row count | Unused | | `OpRuntimeMetrics.bytes_task_outputs_generated` | Total output bytes | Unused | ### 3.3 Three Missing Key Capabilities 1. **Systematic collection and propagation of statistics** — currently `infer_metadata()` returns `BlockMetadata(None, None, None, None)` for most operators 2. **Cost model** — does not exist 3. **Cost-based decision logic** — all rules use if-else pattern matching --- ## 4. Design ### 4.1 Overall Architecture ```mermaid graph TB subgraph Compile Time A[LogicalPlan] --> B[Statistics Propagation] B --> C[Logical Optimization RBO Rules] C --> D[Plan Conversion] D --> E[Physical Optimization RBO Rules] E --> F[CBO: DeriveReservationRatioRule] E --> G[CBO: DeriveShufflePartitionsRule] F --> H[PhysicalPlan] G --> H end subgraph Runtime H --> I[StreamingExecutor] I --> J[OpRuntimeMetrics] J --> K[RuntimeFeedbackCollector] K -.->|Next Execution| B end ``` CBO consists of four modules: | Module | Responsibility | Phase | |--------|---------------|-------| | **Statistics Layer** (`OperatorStatistics`) | Collect, propagate, and estimate data statistics | Before logical optimization | | **Cost Model** (`CostEstimator`) | Quantify resource consumption per operator | Physical optimization | | **Parameter Derivation Rules** | Derive R, num_partitions, and other parameters | Physical optimization | | **Runtime Feedback** | Collect actual metrics to correct estimates | Post-execution | ### 4.2 Statistics Layer Design #### 4.2.1 Data Structures ```python from dataclasses import dataclass, field from typing import Optional, Dict @dataclass class ColumnStatistics: """Per-column statistics""" name: str # Available directly from Parquet footer (zero cost) min_value: Optional[any] = None max_value: Optional[any] = None null_count: Optional[int] = None distinct_count: Optional[int] = None # NDV # Requires sampling or computation avg_size_bytes: Optional[float] = None # Parquet column encoding information encoding: Optional[str] = None compression: Optional[str] = None @dataclass class OperatorStatistics: """Operator-level statistics, propagated along the DAG""" # Basic statistics num_rows: Optional[int] = None size_bytes: Optional[int] = None num_blocks: Optional[int] = None avg_row_bytes: Optional[float] = None # Column-level statistics column_stats: Dict[str, ColumnStatistics] = field(default_factory=dict) # Selectivity estimate (Filter operator specific) selectivity: Optional[float] = None # 0.0 ~ 1.0 # Amplification/reduction ratio (Map operator specific) amplification_ratio: Optional[float] = None # output_rows / input_rows # Data skew factor (Join/Shuffle operator specific) skew_factor: Optional[float] = None # max_partition_size / avg_partition_size # Confidence (indicates reliability of the statistics) confidence: float = 1.0 # 1.0 = exact, <1.0 = estimated def scale(self, ratio: float) -> "OperatorStatistics": """Scale proportionally (for post-predicate-pushdown statistics propagation)""" return OperatorStatistics( num_rows=int(self.num_rows * ratio) if self.num_rows else None, size_bytes=int(self.size_bytes * ratio) if self.size_bytes else None, num_blocks=self.num_blocks, avg_row_bytes=self.avg_row_bytes, column_stats=self.column_stats, selectivity=ratio, confidence=self.confidence * 0.9, # Propagation reduces confidence ) ``` **Design decisions**: - **Confidence field**: The longer the propagation chain, the less reliable the estimates. The `confidence` field allows downstream decision logic to adjust strategy based on reliability (low confidence → more conservative fallback). - **Separate selectivity and amplification ratio**: Filter and Map have different statistics propagation semantics; separating them avoids confusion. - **Skew factor**: Data skew in Join/Shuffle scenarios leads to uneven memory demand, which is a critical input for reservation ratio derivation. #### 4.2.2 Three-Layer Acquisition Strategy ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Layer 3: Runtime Feedback │ │ Previous execution's OpRuntimeMetrics → correct │ │ compile-time estimates │ │ Trigger: ~/.ray/data/stats_cache/<plan_hash>.json │ │ exists │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Layer 2: Sampling Estimation │ │ First batch avg_row_bytes / schema → propagate │ │ estimates │ │ Trigger: Non-Parquet data sources │ ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Layer 1: Metadata Direct Read │ │ Parquet footer / Hive partition list → zero-cost │ │ acquisition │ │ Trigger: Parquet data source (default path) │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Layer 1 implementation details — extracting column-level statistics from Parquet Footer**: The `RowGroup → Column → Statistics` structure in the Parquet footer contains min/max/null_count/distinct_count, but Ray Data only uses `num_rows` in `_fetch_parquet_file_info`. Extension approach: ```python # New method, source location: python/ray/data/_internal/datasource/parquet_datasource.py def _extract_column_stats_from_parquet( metadata: "pyarrow._parquet.FileMetaData", ) -> Dict[str, ColumnStatistics]: """Extract column-level statistics from Parquet FileMetaData (zero additional IO).""" column_stats = {} schema = metadata.schema.to_arrow_schema() for col_idx in range(metadata.num_columns): col_name = schema.field(col_idx).name # Aggregate statistics across all RowGroups total_null_count = 0 global_min, global_max = None, None for rg_idx in range(metadata.num_row_groups): col_meta = metadata.row_group(rg_idx).column(col_idx) if col_meta.statistics is not None: stats = col_meta.statistics if stats.has_min_max: if global_min is None or stats.min < global_min: global_min = stats.min if global_max is None or stats.max > global_max: global_max = stats.max if stats.null_count is not None: total_null_count += stats.null_count column_stats[col_name] = ColumnStatistics( name=col_name, min_value=global_min, max_value=global_max, null_count=total_null_count, distinct_count=col_meta.statistics.distinct_count if col_meta.statistics and col_meta.statistics.distinct_count else None, compression=str(col_meta.compression), ) return column_stats ``` #### 4.2.3 Statistics Propagation Rules Each logical operator type must define its "transform function" for statistics: | Operator | Propagation Rule | Confidence Decay | |----------|-----------------|:----------------:| | **Read** | Directly from Parquet footer or sampling | 0.95 | | **Filter** | `output = input.scale(selectivity)` | ×0.9 | | **Project** | `num_rows` unchanged, `size_bytes` scaled by column ratio | ×0.95 | | **Map** | Scale based on `amplification_ratio` (default 1.0) | ×0.8 | | **Join** | `rows = |L| × |R| / max(NDV_L, NDV_R)` | ×0.7 | | **Sort** | Row count unchanged, `size_bytes` unchanged | ×1.0 | | **Limit** | `num_rows = min(input_rows, limit)` | ×1.0 | | **Union** | Sum of statistics from all branches | ×1.0 | **Selectivity estimation** (referencing classic databases + Spark CBO): ```python def _estimate_selectivity(predicate: Expr, stats: OperatorStatistics) -> float: """ Selectivity estimation rules: - Equality predicate: 1 / NDV - Range predicate: (max - val) / (max - min) - is_in predicate: len(values) / NDV - AND: selectivity(A) × selectivity(B) (independence assumption) - OR: 1 - (1 - sel(A)) × (1 - sel(B)) - Cannot estimate: fall back to 0.5 """ ``` **Trade-off TD-1: Independence assumption** — AND compound predicates assume columns are mutually independent. This often does not hold in practice (e.g., `age > 18 AND income > 50000` have positive correlation), but introducing correlation coefficients requires histogram support, which is too costly. Fallback strategy: use conservative default values when statistics are unavailable (equality 0.1, range 0.33, unknown 0.5). ### 4.3 Cost Model Design #### 4.3.1 Vector Cost vs Scalar Cost | Approach | Advantages | Disadvantages | |----------|-----------|---------------| | **Scalar cost** (Spark approach, single number) | Simple, easy to compare | Cannot express heterogeneous resources: CPU/GPU/Memory/Network | | **Vector cost** (this proposal) | Precisely describes resource consumption across dimensions | Comparison requires weighting, introducing subjectivity in weight selection | **Decision**: Adopt vector cost. Rationale: Ray Data runs on heterogeneous clusters (CPU + GPU), and the core goal of CBO is to derive `reservation_ratio` (a memory-dimension parameter). The vector model can directly read the `peak_memory_bytes` dimension without losing information through scalar conversion. ```python @dataclass class OperatorCost: """Per-operator cost vector""" cpu_cost: float = 0.0 # CPU cores × seconds gpu_cost: float = 0.0 # GPU cores × seconds io_read_bytes: float = 0.0 # Bytes read io_write_bytes: float = 0.0 # Bytes written peak_memory_bytes: float = 0.0 # Peak memory usage object_store_bytes: float = 0.0 # Object Store usage shuffle_bytes: float = 0.0 # Cross-node transfer bytes def total_weighted_cost(self, weights: "CostWeights" = None) -> float: """Weighted total cost, used for plan comparison (e.g., Join Reorder)""" w = weights or CostWeights() return ( self.cpu_cost * w.cpu + self.gpu_cost * w.gpu + self.io_read_bytes * w.io_read + self.io_write_bytes * w.io_write + self.peak_memory_bytes * w.memory + self.object_store_bytes * w.object_store + self.shuffle_bytes * w.shuffle ) def add(self, other: "OperatorCost") -> "OperatorCost": return OperatorCost( cpu_cost=self.cpu_cost + other.cpu_cost, gpu_cost=self.gpu_cost + other.gpu_cost, io_read_bytes=self.io_read_bytes + other.io_read_bytes, io_write_bytes=self.io_write_bytes + other.io_write_bytes, peak_memory_bytes=max(self.peak_memory_bytes, other.peak_memory_bytes), object_store_bytes=self.object_store_bytes + other.object_store_bytes, shuffle_bytes=self.shuffle_bytes + other.shuffle_bytes, ) @dataclass class CostWeights: """Cost weights, adjustable based on cluster characteristics""" cpu: float = 1.0 gpu: float = 10.0 # GPU is more expensive than CPU io_read: float = 0.001 io_write: float = 0.002 memory: float = 0.0001 object_store: float = 0.0002 shuffle: float = 0.005 # Network transfer is the most expensive ``` **Trade-off TD-2: `peak_memory_bytes` uses `max` semantics** — Operators in the pipeline execute concurrently, and peak memory is determined by the largest one. Using `max` rather than `sum` better reflects reality. However, when multiple operators are simultaneously active, the actual peak may approach `sum`. Fallback strategy: `ReservationRatioDeriver` uses `memory_demands[op] = max(peak_memory, object_store / N)` as a conservative estimate. #### 4.3.2 Per-Operator Cost Formulas | Operator | CPU | GPU | IO Read | Memory Peak | Object Store | Shuffle | |----------|-----|-----|---------|-------------|-------------|---------| | Read | rows × 0.00001 | 0 | size_bytes | 0 | size_bytes | 0 | | Filter | rows × 0.000005 | 0 | 0 | 0 | output_bytes | 0 | | Map | rows × 0.0001 | rows × 0.00005 (if GPU) | 0 | avg_row_bytes × 4096 | output_bytes | 0 | | Join | (L_rows + R_rows) × 0.0001 | 0 | 0 | partition_bytes × 3 | input_bytes + output_bytes | total_input_bytes | | Sort | n × log₂(n) × 0.000001 | 0 | 0 | input_bytes | input_bytes × 2 | input_bytes | > Join's `partition_bytes × 3` source: references `JoiningOperator._estimate_aggregator_memory_allocation` formula — shuffle_memory + join_memory (2x PyArrow overhead) + output_memory. **Trade-off TD-3: Cost coefficient calibration** — The coefficients above (0.00001, etc.) are based on empirical values and vary significantly across hardware. No automatic calibration mechanism is introduced for now; `CostWeights` provides tunable knobs. Phase 4 runtime feedback can provide calibration data. ### 4.4 Reservation Ratio Auto-Derivation #### 4.4.1 Problem Formalization Given an execution plan and statistics, automatically compute the optimal `R` value such that: - **Constraint 1**: No operator is frequently backpressured due to insufficient memory (avoid starvation) - **Constraint 2**: Maximize resource utilization (avoid idleness) #### 4.4.2 Derivation Algorithm ```python class ReservationRatioDeriver: """Auto-derive reservation ratio based on cost model""" @staticmethod def derive( op_costs: Dict[str, OperatorCost], cluster_resources: "ExecutionResources", pipeline_properties: "PipelineProperties", ) -> float: """ Derive optimal reservation ratio R. Core idea: R should reflect the imbalance in resource demands across operators. - All operators have equal demands → competition is fair, low R suffices - One operator demands 10x others → needs high R to prevent starvation """ n_ops = len(op_costs) if n_ops <= 1: return 0.3 # Single operator, no competition # Step 1: Compute each operator's "ideal memory share" memory_demands = {} for op_name, cost in op_costs.items(): memory_demands[op_name] = max( cost.peak_memory_bytes, cost.object_store_bytes / n_ops, # Amortize Object Store ) total_demand = sum(memory_demands.values()) if total_demand == 0: return 0.5 # Fall back to default # Step 2: Compute demand imbalance coefficient avg_demand = total_demand / n_ops max_demand = max(memory_demands.values()) imbalance_ratio = max_demand / avg_demand if avg_demand > 0 else 1.0 # Step 3: Derive R based on imbalance coefficient # imbalance = 1.0 (perfectly balanced) → R = 0.3 # imbalance = 5.0 (severely imbalanced) → R = 0.8 r_base = 0.3 r_imbalance = min(0.5, (imbalance_ratio - 1.0) * 0.1) # Step 4: Pipeline characteristic adjustments r_pipeline = 0.0 if n_ops >= 5: # Long pipeline bonus r_pipeline += 0.05 * min(n_ops - 4, 4) if pipeline_properties.has_gpu_ops: # GPU operator bonus r_pipeline += 0.1 if pipeline_properties.has_alltoall_ops: # AllToAll discount r_pipeline -= 0.1 if max_demand > total_demand * 0.7: # Single-operator dominance discount r_pipeline -= 0.15 r_final = max(0.1, min(0.9, r_base + r_imbalance + r_pipeline)) return round(r_final, 2) @dataclass class PipelineProperties: """Pipeline characteristics summary""" has_gpu_ops: bool = False has_alltoall_ops: bool = False has_shuffle_ops: bool = False num_stages: int = 0 is_spot_environment: bool = False ``` #### 4.4.3 Derivation Validation | Scenario | Pipeline Structure | Key Parameters | Derived R | Manual Empirical Value | Deviation | |----------|-------------------|----------------|-----------|----------------------|-----------| | Long pipeline + GPU | Read→Filter→Join→Feature→Model(GPU)→Write | N=5, GPU=Y | 0.61 | 0.6~0.7 | <0.05 | | Short pipeline + batch inference | Read→Model(GPU)→Write | N=2, GPU=Y | 0.33 | 0.2~0.3 | ~0.05 | | Sort pipeline | Read→Map→Sort→Write | N=3, AllToAll=Y | 0.21 | 0.2~0.3 | <0.05 | **Validation walkthrough (Scenario 1)**: ``` op_costs = { Read: peak_memory=2GiB, object_store=10GiB Filter: peak_memory=512MiB, object_store=3GiB Join: peak_memory=8GiB, object_store=6GiB Feature: peak_memory=1GiB, object_store=3GiB Model: peak_memory=4GiB, gpu_cost=100 } memory_demands: Read=2G, Filter=0.6G, Join=8G, Feature=1G, Model=4G avg_demand = 3.12G, max_demand = 8G imbalance_ratio = 8 / 3.12 = 2.56 r_base = 0.3 r_imbalance = min(0.5, (2.56-1) × 0.1) = 0.156 r_pipeline = 0.05×(5-4) + 0.1(GPU) = 0.15 r_final = 0.3 + 0.156 + 0.15 = 0.606 → 0.61 ``` #### 4.4.4 Integration as a Physical Optimization Rule ```python class DeriveReservationRatioRule(Rule): """CBO rule: auto-derive reservation ratio Registered in the physical optimization phase, executed after FuseOperators. Reason: operator fusion changes the number of operators and resource demands, so derivation must happen after fusion is complete. """ @classmethod def dependencies(cls) -> List[Type["Rule"]]: return [FuseOperators] def apply(self, plan: PhysicalPlan) -> PhysicalPlan: # 1. Collect statistics for each physical operator statistics_cache = self._collect_statistics(plan) # 2. Estimate cost for each operator op_costs = self._estimate_costs(plan, statistics_cache) # 3. Extract pipeline characteristics pipeline_props = self._extract_pipeline_properties(plan) # 4. Derive reservation ratio cluster_resources = self._get_cluster_resources() derived_ratio = ReservationRatioDeriver.derive( op_costs, cluster_resources, pipeline_props ) # 5. Only override when user has not explicitly set it if not plan.context._user_set_reservation_ratio: plan.context.op_resource_reservation_ratio = derived_ratio logger.info( f"CBO derived reservation_ratio={derived_ratio} " f"(pipeline: {pipeline_props.num_stages} stages, " f"gpu={pipeline_props.has_gpu_ops}, " f"alltoall={pipeline_props.has_alltoall_ops})" ) return plan ``` ### 4.5 CBO Extension Rules #### 4.5.1 Join Reorder ```python class JoinReorderRule(Rule): """CBO rule: automatic multi-table Join reordering Strategy: Place the smaller table on the build side (right), larger table on the probe side (left). Limitation: Only applies to INNER JOIN (other types change semantics when sides swap). """ def apply(self, plan: LogicalPlan) -> LogicalPlan: dag = plan.dag new_dag = dag._apply_transform(self._try_reorder_join) return LogicalPlan(new_dag, plan.context) if dag is not new_dag else plan def _try_reorder_join(self, op: LogicalOperator) -> LogicalOperator: if not isinstance(op, Join) or op._join_type != JoinType.INNER: return op left_stats = op.input_dependencies[0].infer_statistics() right_stats = op.input_dependencies[1].infer_statistics() if (left_stats.size_bytes and right_stats.size_bytes and left_stats.size_bytes < right_stats.size_bytes): return self._swap_join_sides(op) return op ``` **Trade-off TD-4: INNER JOIN only** — Swapping sides for LEFT/RIGHT/FULL JOIN changes semantics. In theory, equivalent transformations are possible (e.g., LEFT → RIGHT + column swap), but the complexity is high and error-prone. Only INNER JOIN is supported for now. #### 4.5.2 Auto-Derive num_partitions ```python class DeriveShufflePartitionsRule(Rule): """CBO rule: auto-derive Shuffle partition count Goal: Keep each partition's data volume between 256MB ~ 1GB - Too small: High task scheduling overhead, too many Aggregator Actors - Too large: Single-partition Join memory exceeds limit, OOM risk """ TARGET_PARTITION_SIZE_BYTES = 512 * 1024 * 1024 # 512MB MIN_PARTITIONS = 10 MAX_PARTITIONS = 10000 def apply(self, plan: PhysicalPlan) -> PhysicalPlan: for op in plan.dag.post_order_iter(): if isinstance(op, HashShufflingOperatorBase): self._derive_partitions(op, plan) return plan def _derive_partitions(self, op, plan): total_input_bytes = _try_estimate_output_bytes(op._logical_operators) if total_input_bytes is None: return # Statistics unavailable, skip derivation ideal_partitions = max( self.MIN_PARTITIONS, min(self.MAX_PARTITIONS, int(total_input_bytes / self.TARGET_PARTITION_SIZE_BYTES)) ) # Only override when user has not explicitly set it if not getattr(op, '_user_set_num_partitions', False): op._num_partitions = ideal_partitions ``` **Trade-off TD-5: Fixed target partition size of 512MB** — Different hardware and operators (Hash Join vs Sort) have different optimal partition sizes. A uniform 512MB is used for now; it can later be exposed as a `DataContext` configuration. ### 4.6 Runtime Feedback ```python class RuntimeFeedbackCollector: """Collect runtime statistics to correct CBO estimates for the next execution Storage path: ~/.ray/data/stats_cache/<plan_hash>.json Cache policy: LRU, max 100 entries """ @staticmethod def collect_feedback(plan: PhysicalPlan) -> Dict[str, Dict]: feedback = {} for op in plan.dag.post_order_iter(): metrics = op.metrics feedback[op.name] = { "actual_rows": metrics.rows_task_outputs_generated, "actual_bytes": metrics.bytes_task_outputs_generated, "actual_avg_bytes_per_output": metrics.average_bytes_per_output, "actual_wall_time": metrics.task_completion_time_total_s, } return feedback @staticmethod def apply_feedback( stats: OperatorStatistics, feedback: Dict, ) -> OperatorStatistics: """Correct statistics using runtime feedback (exponential moving average)""" if "actual_rows" in feedback and feedback["actual_rows"]: alpha = 0.7 # Weight for actual values if stats.num_rows: stats.num_rows = int( alpha * feedback["actual_rows"] + (1 - alpha) * stats.num_rows ) stats.confidence = min(stats.confidence + 0.2, 1.0) return stats ``` **Trade-off TD-6: Cache based on plan_hash** — Identical logical plans share runtime feedback. However, changes in data volume (e.g., 10GB yesterday, 100GB today) can invalidate the cache. Fallback strategy: the feedback weight alpha=0.7 means new data dominates, old cache influence is only 30%, preventing severe deviation. --- ## 5. Trade-off and Decision Records | ID | Decision Point | Choice | Rationale | Alternative | Risk | |----|---------------|--------|-----------|-------------|------| | TD-1 | AND compound predicate selectivity | Independence assumption | Histogram cost too high | Introduce correlation coefficient matrix | Selectivity underestimated for correlated columns | | TD-2 | Pipeline total peak_memory | `max` semantics | Operators execute alternately | `sum` semantics | Underestimation when multiple operators are concurrently active | | TD-3 | Cost coefficients | Fixed empirical values | Simplification for v1 | Automatic calibration | Large deviation across different hardware | | TD-4 | Join Reorder scope | INNER JOIN only | Semantic safety | Support all Join types | INNER JOIN has high share, limited impact | | TD-5 | Target partition size | Fixed 512MB | Simplify implementation | Adaptive based on operator type | May be too small for Sort, too large for Join | | TD-6 | Feedback cache granularity | plan_hash | Simple implementation | plan_hash + data_hash | Cache invalidation when data volume changes dramatically | | TD-7 | Statistics storage location | `LogicalOperator` method | Minimal intrusion | Standalone `StatisticsStore` | Query requires DAG traversal | | TD-8 | CBO toggle | Enabled by default, user settings take priority | Seamless upgrade | Disabled by default, requires manual enablement | Regression risk requires thorough testing | --- ## 6. Known Issues and Risks ### 6.1 Estimation Accuracy Issues | Issue | Impact | Mitigation | |-------|--------|------------| | **Parquet distinct_count is unreliable** | Many Parquet writers do not write distinct_count | Fall back to heuristic (e.g., `num_rows * 0.5`) | | **Independence assumption failure** | AND selectivity severely underestimated for correlated columns | Conservative defaults (0.5); no aggressive optimization when confidence is low | | **Map operator amplification ratio unknown** | UDF may be 1:N or N:1 | Default `amplification_ratio = 1.0`, corrected by runtime feedback | | **Compression ratio discrepancy** | Parquet size_bytes (on disk) vs in-memory size differ significantly | Use `avg_row_in_mem_bytes` (already available) instead of on-disk size | ### 6.2 Regression Risks | Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation | |------|------------|--------|------------| | CBO-derived R is worse than default 0.5 | Medium | Performance degradation | Add A/B testing framework in Phase 2; `_user_set_reservation_ratio` guarantees user override | | Bug in statistics propagation chain causing `num_rows = 0` | Low | Derivation fails, falls back to default | All `scale()` operations check for None; cost model handles 0 values | | Parquet footer reading slows down (extremely large number of files) | Low | `get_execution_plan` latency increase | Parquet footer is already read in existing path, no new IO added | | `Expressions` API change breaks selectivity estimation | Medium | Selectivity falls back to default values | Loosely coupled design; `_estimate_selectivity` catches all exceptions and returns 0.5 | ### 6.3 Uncovered Scenarios 1. **Non-Parquet data sources** (CSV, JSON, custom Datasource): Layer 1 unavailable, relies on Layer 2 sampling. If sampling is also unavailable, falls back to RBO. 2. **Dynamic data sources** (streaming input, Delta Lake Time Travel): Statistics cache may become stale. Requires version number or timestamp invalidation mechanism (to be considered in Phase 4). 3. **Multi-pipeline concurrency**: CBO does not account for resource usage by other pipelines. Overlaps with `ExecutionOptions.exclude_resources` but is out of scope for this proposal. --- ## 7. Implementation Plan ### 7.1 General Principles 1. **Backward compatible**: CBO only takes effect when the user has not explicitly set parameters 2. **Incremental introduction**: Start with the simplest statistics, expand gradually 3. **Minimal intrusion**: Leverage existing `Rule/Optimizer/Ruleset` interfaces, no changes to the execution engine 4. **Observable**: All CBO decisions are logged at INFO level for easy debugging ### 7.2 Phase 1: Statistics Infrastructure (2~3 weeks) **Goal**: Enable logical operators to "see" basic data characteristics. **Changed files**: ``` New: python/ray/data/_internal/stats/operator_statistics.py # OperatorStatistics data structure Modified: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/interfaces/logical_operator.py # Add infer_statistics() python/ray/data/_internal/logical/operators/read_operator.py # Implement Read statistics inference python/ray/data/_internal/logical/operators/one_to_one_operator.py # Filter/Limit statistics propagation python/ray/data/_internal/logical/operators/all_to_all_operator.py # Sort/Repartition statistics propagation python/ray/data/_internal/logical/operators/n_ary_operator.py # Join/Union statistics propagation python/ray/data/_internal/datasource/parquet_datasource.py # Extract column stats from footer New tests: python/ray/data/tests/test_operator_statistics.py ``` **Acceptance criteria**: 1. `Read(Parquet)`'s `infer_statistics()` returns `OperatorStatistics` containing `num_rows`, `size_bytes`, and column-level min/max 2. `Filter` operator's `infer_statistics()` returns selectivity-scaled statistics 3. All operators' `infer_statistics()` return `OperatorStatistics()` when statistics are unavailable, rather than raising exceptions 4. `ds.explain()` can display a statistics summary for each operator ### 7.3 Phase 2: Cost Model and Reservation Ratio Derivation (2~3 weeks) **Goal**: Auto-derive `reservation_ratio` based on statistics. **Changed files**: ``` New: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/cost_model.py # OperatorCost + CostEstimator python/ray/data/_internal/logical/rules/derive_reservation_ratio.py # DeriveReservationRatioRule Modified: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/optimizers.py # Register new rule in _PHYSICAL_RULESET python/ray/data/context.py # Add _user_set_reservation_ratio flag python/ray/data/_internal/execution/__init__.py # create_resource_allocator reads derived value New tests: python/ray/data/tests/test_cbo_reservation_ratio.py ``` **Rule registration**: ```python # optimizers.py modification _PHYSICAL_RULESET = Ruleset([ InheritTargetMaxBlockSizeRule, SetReadParallelismRule, FuseOperators, ConfigureMapTaskMemoryUsingOutputSize, DeriveReservationRatioRule, # New: declares dependencies=[FuseOperators] ]) ``` **Acceptance criteria**: 1. When `reservation_ratio` is not manually set, CBO auto-derives and writes to `DataContext` 2. When `reservation_ratio` is manually set, CBO does not override 3. Derived values for three standard scenarios (long pipeline + GPU, short pipeline + batch inference, Sort pipeline) deviate ≤ 0.05 from manual empirical values 4. Log outputs `CBO derived reservation_ratio=X.XX (pipeline: N stages, gpu=T/F, alltoall=T/F)` ### 7.4 Phase 3: Shuffle Partition Derivation + Join Reorder (3~4 weeks) **Goal**: Auto-derive `num_partitions`; automatic INNER JOIN reordering. **Changed files**: ``` New: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/rules/derive_shuffle_partitions.py python/ray/data/_internal/logical/rules/join_reorder.py Modified: python/ray/data/_internal/logical/optimizers.py # Register new rules New tests: python/ray/data/tests/test_cbo_shuffle_partitions.py python/ray/data/tests/test_cbo_join_reorder.py ``` **Acceptance criteria**: 1. A Join with 10GB input data auto-derives `num_partitions ≈ 20` (10GB / 512MB) 2. The smaller table in INNER JOIN is automatically placed on the build side (right) 3. When the user explicitly sets `num_partitions`, CBO does not override 4. Non-INNER JOINs do not trigger JoinReorder ### 7.5 Phase 4: Runtime Feedback Loop (4~6 weeks) **Goal**: Use `OpRuntimeMetrics` from previous executions to correct compile-time estimates. **Changed files**: ``` New: python/ray/data/_internal/stats/runtime_feedback.py # RuntimeFeedbackCollector Modified: python/ray/data/_internal/execution/streaming_executor.py # Call collect_feedback after execution New tests: python/ray/data/tests/test_runtime_feedback.py ``` **Acceptance criteria**: 1. After the first execution, a JSON cache file is generated under `~/.ray/data/stats_cache/` 2. On the second execution of the same pipeline, CBO uses the cache to correct statistics 3. LRU cache eviction works correctly (max 100 entries) 4. Cache does not affect execution of different pipelines ### 7.6 Implementation Timeline ```mermaid graph LR P1["Phase 1: Statistics Infrastructure 2~3 weeks"] P2["Phase 2: Cost Model + Reservation Derivation 2~3 weeks"] P3["Phase 3: Shuffle + Join Optimization 3~4 weeks"] P4["Phase 4: Runtime Feedback 4~6 weeks"] P1 --> P2 P2 --> P3 P3 --> P4 ``` | Phase | Core Deliverable | User-Perceivable Benefit | Independently Releasable | |-------|-----------------|-------------------------|:------------------------:| | Phase 1 | `OperatorStatistics` + propagation chain | `ds.explain()` displays statistics | Yes | | Phase 2 | `DeriveReservationRatioRule` | Auto-derive reservation ratio, eliminate manual tuning | Yes | | Phase 3 | `DeriveShufflePartitionsRule` + `JoinReorderRule` | Join/Shuffle performance auto-optimization | Yes | | Phase 4 | `RuntimeFeedbackCollector` | Repeated executions get faster | Yes | --- ## 8. Comparison with Spark Catalyst ### 8.1 Architecture Comparison | Dimension | Spark Catalyst | Ray Data CBO (This Proposal) | |-----------|---------------|------------------------------| | Statistics collection timing | Requires explicit `ANALYZE TABLE` command | Automatically from Parquet footer (zero cost) | | Statistics storage | Hive Metastore / Catalog | In-memory temporary structures, optional disk cache | | Cost model dimensions | Single scalar value (cpu + io weighted) | Multi-dimensional vector (CPU/GPU/IO/Memory/Shuffle) | | Core optimization target | Minimize IO + CPU | Minimize memory contention + maximize pipeline throughput | | Resource scheduling integration | None (decoupled from YARN/K8s) | Directly derives `reservation_ratio` affecting resource allocation | | Runtime adaptation | AQE (checkpoints inserted at stage boundaries) | `OpRuntimeMetrics` collected at task level (finer granularity) | | GPU awareness | Not supported | Native GPU cost estimation support | ### 8.2 Why Ray Data CBO Can Be "Lighter" 1. **No Catalog required**: Spark depends on Hive Metastore for statistics storage; Ray Data reads Parquet footer directly, with no external system dependency. 2. **More focused optimization target**: Spark needs to optimize the entire SQL plan tree; Ray Data only needs to optimize resource allocation parameters and Shuffle parameters — "fewer but more precise". 3. **More direct runtime feedback**: Spark AQE needs checkpoints inserted at stage boundaries; Ray Data's `OpRuntimeMetrics` are already collected at the task level, with zero additional cost. --- ## 9. Future Evolution 1. **Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)**: When runtime discovers that statistics significantly deviate from compile-time estimates, dynamically adjust the reservation ratio during execution. `ResourceManager.get_global_limits()` already refreshes every second; in theory, `reservation_ratio` can be incorporated into dynamic refresh. 2. **Statistics cache invalidation**: Parquet data may be updated (e.g., Delta Lake). When should the statistics cache be invalidated? Requires a version number or timestamp-based invalidation mechanism. 3. **Multi-tenant scenarios**: When multiple Ray Data pipelines share a cluster, CBO needs to account for "resource usage by other pipelines". This overlaps with `ExecutionOptions.exclude_resources`. 4. **Statistics as a first-class citizen**: In the long run, `OperatorStatistics` should become a first-class property of `LogicalOperator` (similar to Spark's `LogicalPlan.stats`), rather than an add-on method. 5. **Histogram support**: Introduce equi-frequency/equi-width histograms to improve accuracy of the independence assumption and data skew estimation. --- ## Appendix A: Core Source Code Path Index | Module | Path | Key Classes/Functions | |--------|------|----------------------| | Optimizer architecture | `python/ray/data/_internal/logical/optimizers.py` | `get_execution_plan`, `_LOGICAL_RULESET`, `_PHYSICAL_RULESET` | | Rule/Optimizer interface | `python/ray/data/_internal/logical/interfaces/optimizer.py` | `Rule`, `Optimizer` | | Ruleset | `python/ray/data/_internal/logical/ruleset.py` | `Ruleset._build_graph` | | Logical operator base class | `python/ray/data/_internal/logical/interfaces/logical_operator.py` | `LogicalOperator.infer_metadata`, `estimated_num_outputs` | | Read operator | `python/ray/data/_internal/logical/operators/read_operator.py` | `Read.infer_metadata`, `_estimate_num_outputs` | | Reservation allocation algorithm | `python/ray/data/_internal/execution/resource_manager.py` | `ReservationOpResourceAllocator.update_budgets` | | Runtime metrics | `python/ray/data/_internal/execution/interfaces/op_runtime_metrics.py` | `OpRuntimeMetrics.average_bytes_per_output` | | Parquet metadata | `python/ray/data/_internal/datasource/parquet_datasource.py` | `_ParquetFileInfo`, `_fetch_parquet_file_info` | | Block metadata | `python/ray/data/block.py` | `BlockMetadata`, `BlockExecStats` | | Global configuration | `python/ray/data/context.py` | `DataContext.op_resource_reservation_ratio` | | Expression system | `python/ray/data/expressions.py` | `BinaryExpr`, `ColumnExpr`, `Operation` | | Resource allocator creation | `python/ray/data/_internal/execution/__init__.py` | `create_resource_allocator` | ### Use case _No response_

signals.title: [Data] Optimize triple loop in default_autoscaling_coordinator.py
signals.text: ### Description **What is the problem?** This issue addresses a resource-allocation performance bottleneck in Ray Data autoscaling. **Current code issues** Previously, the coordinator used a triple nested loop when reallocating resources (requesters × requested bundles × cluster nodes). That made allocation cost grow quickly as concurrency increased, causing unnecessary CPU overhead and slower autoscaler reaction times. It was especially inefficient for repeated identical bundles, which were rescanned across nodes from the beginning each time. ### Use case _No response_
signals.author: weimingdiit

signals.title: [Data] Refactor: Checkpoint loading from broadcast-join to bucket-join style
signals.text: ## Problem Current checkpoint restore behaves like a **broadcast join**: the full checkpoint (all checkpointed IDs) is loaded once, and the same block ref is passed to every read task via `checkpointed_ids`. Each task filters its input block against this full ID set. **Impact:** - **Slow filtering**: Each task does a full scan / binary search over the entire checkpointed ID set; with large checkpoints this dominates runtime. - **High memory and OOM risk**: Every read task holds a reference to the full checkpoint block; memory scales with parallelism and can cause OOM. - **Resource underutilization**: Downstream operators (e.g. GPU map/write) hold resources but are starved when the read stage is the bottleneck. Goal: switch to a **bucket-join style** so each read task only receives the checkpoint slice for the source path(s) it reads. ## Design principles - **Simplicity**: Keep the checkpoint loading and filtering logic as straightforward as possible. Use the smallest amount of code to load the existing artifacts from checkpoint_path and apply only the necessary, direct filtering. Avoid introducing new branches, new protocols, or multi-step workflows. - **Minimal dependency**: No new config or storage contract; extend existing `checkpoint_path` and infer layout from its contents. - **Backward compatibility**: Flat layout (no subdirs under `checkpoint_path`) keeps current “single full load” behavior. ## Proposed approach: Bucket by source path, load by bucket Partition checkpoint data by a **bucket key** derived from the read source (e.g. file path or directory). - **Write path**: Write checkpoint files under `checkpoint_path/<bucket_key>/` instead of a single flat directory. Rows are grouped by source path (or directory) when writing. - **Load path**: Before execution, each read task’s input paths are known (e.g. from `ReadTask.metadata.input_files`). Load only the checkpoint subdir(s) for those paths and pass each task only the block ref(s) for its bucket(s). **Outcome:** - Each read task gets only the checkpoint slice for its inputs → lower memory per task and faster filtering. - Layout detection: if `checkpoint_path` has subdirectories, use per-bucket loading; otherwise, keep the current single full load (flat layout). ## Compatibility with other datasources (e.g. Kafka) The design only requires a **bucket key** per read task, derived from whatever the datasource puts in `ReadTask.metadata.input_files` (not necessarily a file path): - **Parquet**: `input_files` are file paths; bucket key can be derived from path or parent directory. - **Kafka**: Datasource already sets `input_files` (e.g. `kafka://topic/partition_id`); the same field can be used to derive the bucket key (e.g. by topic or topic+partition). So the load path is compatible with any datasource that sets `input_files`; the write path must bucket checkpoint data using the same key convention. ### Use case _No response_
signals.author: dragongu

signals.title: [Data] Support predicate pushdown at Delta Lake level
signals.text: ### Description Instead of immediately resolving the parquet file URIs from a DeltaLake table, defer their resolution until execution to enable filtering based on the delta table metadata. This would likely involve a new DeltaDatasource. ### Use case Currently when using `read_delta`, the table is immediately resolved to a list of parquet URIs that are passed into `read_parquet`. If the dataset does not use Hive partitioning, but rather Delta's built-in Z-ordering and table metadata, you end up potentially reading a bunch of unnecessary files, even if it's just for the tail metadata. What would be preferable is deferring this resolution until the source is actually read, at which point all predicates that have been pushed down to the source can be passed to the `file_uris` call. Other attributes such as the schema could also be [efficiently retrieved](https://delta-io.github.io/delta-rs/usage/examining-table/#schema) using Delta Lake-native methods as opposed to the "bunch of parquet files" mode.
